question: What additional locality, method, taxon, rights, and data-quality evidence does the full Looc Lake article provide, and which parts are suitable for regional species research?

sourceDocument.title: Water Quality Parameters, Freshwater Fish Assemblages and Anthropogenic Disturbances in Looc Lake, Castillejos, Zambales, Philippines
sourceDocument.articleSpecificLicense: Creative Commons Attribution 4.0 International (CC BY 4.0), stated in the PDF copyright footer

access.result: The publisher-indexed PDF text was available for full-text review through the web research reader. A direct shell fetch returned a Cloudflare challenge; no challenge was bypassed and no local PDF was retained.
access.scope: Title/citation, abstract, methods, Table 2 text, Table 3 text, figure captions, limitations, conclusion, and copyright/license footer reviewed.
access.visualReview: The PDF was not locally rendered. Text extraction flattened Table 2 presence/absence cells; no species-to-station marks are inferred. Figure 3 images were not visually reviewed.

studyScopeAsReported.coordinateInterpretation: A single publication-reported lake reference coordinate only; independently unverified and not a lake boundary or station coordinate.
studyScopeAsReported.representativeSpecimens: The authors state that representative specimens were brought to a laboratory for further identification and photo-documentation; no voucher/accession crosswalk is supplied in the reviewed article.

quantitativeIntegrity.metric: Eight species relative-abundance percentages in the article's Fish Assemblages results text
quantitativeIntegrity.disposition: Does not reconcile as an exhaustive relative-abundance distribution. Do not use the percentages for charts, ranking, reconstructed counts, or app display. No value was corrected or guessed.

stationTableIntegrity.table2SpeciesByStationPresenceMatrix: The text extraction flattened the east/west/north/south/central cells. Do not assign any named taxon to an individual station from this extraction.

taxonomyAndOriginCrosswalk.crosswalkResult: All eight article names match species entries in the existing Jamandre 2023 Philippine freshwater checklist extraction. That checklist classifies the eight as introduced at a broad Philippine river-basin or island-group scope; this does not independently establish presence or non-native status at Looc Lake.
taxonomyAndOriginCrosswalk.familySpellingIssue: The article prints Osphronomidae for both Trichopodus species; the Jamandre checklist uses Osphronemidae. Preserve the printed value and keep the family normalization explicit.

channaStriataStatusConflict.checklist2023: Introduced to many river basins across the Philippines.
channaStriataStatusConflict.fao1997: The FAO checklist describes Channa striata as native in almost all Philippine freshwater lakes and streams, citing Herre (1953).
channaStriataStatusConflict.resolution: Unresolved and potentially locality-dependent. Do not mark the Looc Lake fish as native, non-native, or invasive from this crosswalk alone.

taxonomyAndOriginCrosswalk.authorClaim: The paper calls all eight species non-native and describes Sarotherodon melanotheron as invasive. Preserve this as an author-reported claim; do not project it as independently verified Looc-specific status.

figureImageReview.sourceFigureLicense: The article PDF states CC BY 4.0 for the article.
figureImageReview.decision: The caption supplies a source-reported label-to-image order, but the figure itself was not visually checked. No photograph was copied or added to src/lib/species-images.ts. Follow the species-image rule and visually verify each asset and retain visible source/license/identification credits before any app reuse.

scopeLimits: One lake, five designated stations, daytime gear-based sampling over one reported bimonthly annual window; this is a local historical study, not a Luzon inventory.
No individual event dates, station coordinates, voucher/accession identifiers, or station-level species assignments were admitted.
The survey's gear selectivity and daylight schedule may miss taxa using other habitats or times.
The paper calls itself preliminary and explicitly limits conclusions to a local baseline rather than causation or wider generalisation.
The article's relative-abundance percentages conflict arithmetically; no correction can be inferred.
The non-native/invasive claims are author-reported and require locality-specific review.

decision.decisionText: Record eight author-reported taxa as historical Looc Lake source candidates with dates, methods, and explicit conflicts. Keep all source claims research-only; do not infer species-by-station distribution, use the inconsistent percentages, classify local invasion status, add lake geometry, or copy the article photos until the specified reviews are complete.

sources.supports: Article metadata, five-station design, 2023-2024 sampling window, the eight reported species and percentages, station totals, limitations, figure caption, and article-specific CC BY 4.0 footer.
Existing checklist extraction crosswalk for the eight names and the checklist's introduced-status statements; national context, not a Looc Lake occurrence source.
Older Philippine checklist's conflicting nationwide native-status statement for Channa striata; not a Looc Lake locality source.
Publisher terms state that open-access articles are licensed by authors and require citation.

nextAction: Continue Central Luzon coverage with other independently sourced waterbodies. Reopen this record only for an official correction/author clarification of the abundance mismatch, a locality-specific C. striata origin decision, station-matrix visual review, or image-level verification. Luzon and Region III remain incomplete.
